Marcus —

Thanks for the ping. High-level legal position: we are comfortable executing customer DPAs, including UK Addendum/IDTA material, provided the terms are commercially reasonable and do not require us to adopt onerous breach notice or audit obligations beyond our standard DPA. For cross-border safeguards we typically offer either:

A) EU SCCs (2021 or updated version as appropriate) + a Redwood TIA annex that documents technical, organizational, and contractual measures (cache residency controls, KV cache scope, encryption-in-transit & at-rest, logging and access controls, subprocessor policy).

B) Customer-supplied TIA/IDTA language: acceptable if redlines are limited. We must not accept open-ended liability increases or perpetual data localization obligations.

On subprocessors: attached is our latest subprocessor inventory (redwood_subprocessors_2025-07.csv). We have one monitoring vendor with support staff in APAC but that vendor processes telemetry (non-customer content logs) only. No APAC-hosted systems process EU customer content currently. We also have US-based vector-db and metrics vendors.

Notification process: we provide 30 days' notice for material subprocessor changes in enterprise contracts, and maintain a published list with a changelog. For Acme, we can commit to the 30-day notice.

Suggested next steps for Marcus:
- Offer Acme option A (SCCs + Redwood TIA annex) and attach our TIA language, with an invitation to call to discuss any specific redlines.
- If Acme insists on their DPA + UK IDTA, ask them to mark any substantive redlines; we will review and propose limited counter language for liability and localization clauses.

I can take the redlines and propose edits if you want me to lead negotiation.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
